name: Bosutinib

fields.mechanism_of_action: Oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that inhibits BCR-ABL kinase (Philadelphia chromosome fusion protein) and SRC-family kinases; inhibits proliferation and induces apoptosis in CML cells — anchored to FDA BOSULIF pharmacology review.
indications: Chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) with Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph+): adult patients in chronic phase (CP) with resistance or intolerance to prior therapy; accelerated phase (AP) or blast phase (BP) — anchored to FDA BOSULIF label.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to bosutinib or any excipients; Pregnancy (embryo-fetal toxicity — use effective contraception); Breast-feeding (discontinue); Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C) — contraindicated; Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers (dose adjustments required, see interactions).
side_effects: Very common (≥20%): diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, thrombocytopenia, anemia, neutropenia, abdominal pain, rash, fatigue, headache, cough, pyrexia, elevated ALT/AST; Common (1–20%): edema, dyspnea, dizziness, arthralgia, back pain, upper respiratory infection; Serious: severe diarrhea (may require hospitalization), severe hematologic toxicity (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia), significant hepatic enzyme elevations, pulmonary toxicity (interstitial pneumonitis), tumor lysis syndrome (in high-burden disease) — anchored to FDA BOSULIF adverse-reactions data.

dosage.adult: Chronic phase (CP): 400 mg orally once daily with food; Accelerated phase (AP) / blast phase (BP): 500 mg orally once daily with food — anchored to FDA BOSULIF label. Dose modifications for hematologic/non-hematologic toxicity per label table.
dosage.geriatric: No specific geriatric dose adjustment; same as adult with caution due to comorbidities and concurrent medications — FDA BOSULIF section 8.5.
dosage.paediatric: Not approved for pediatric use — no established pediatric regimen — FDA BOSULIF section 8.4.

fields.adult_dosing: Chronic phase: 400 mg once daily with food; AP/BP: 500 mg once daily with food — anchored to FDA BOSULIF label. Dose modifications per toxicity: see dosage.adult.
interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir): double dose reduction required (CP: max 300 mg/day; AP/BP: max 400 mg/day); Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine): same dose reduction; Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin): avoid concurrent use or increase dose (CP: up to 600 mg/day; AP/BP: up to 750 mg/day) per label; Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and H2 blockers: avoid concurrent use (decrease solubility/absorption); Antacids: separate by at least 2 hours; Concurrent myelosuppressive agents: additive hematologic toxicity; Concurrent CYP substrates: potential interaction — anchored to FDA BOSULIF interactions table.
monitoring: Complete blood count (platelet count, ANC): baseline, weekly for first month, then monthly; Liver function tests (ALT, AST, total bilirubin): baseline, monthly for first 3 months, then periodically; Diarrhea assessment: at each visit; Signs of dehydration/electrolyte imbalance — treat promptly; Signs of pulmonary toxicity (new cough, dyspnea, hypoxia) — evaluate promptly; Tumor-lysis markers (uric acid, potassium, phosphate, calcium) in high-burden patients at baseline and first month; Pregnancy test: before initiation (if applicable) — anchored to FDA BOSULIF monitoring recommendations.
patient_counselling: Take exactly once daily with food at same time each day; swallow tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or split; report new/worsening diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, rash, fatigue, cough, shortness of breath, or unusual bruising/bleeding; use effective contraception during and for 2 weeks after therapy; avoid concurrent PPIs (e.g. omeprazole) — discuss with clinician; avoid concurrent CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers; store at room temperature, protected from moisture; do not miss doses — if missed, take next dose at regular time (do not double) — anchored to FDA BOSULIF counselling framework.
warnings: Embryo-fetal toxicity (use effective contraception during and for 2 weeks after last dose); Severe diarrhea (manage promptly; consider antidiarrheal treatment, hydration, dose interruption/reduction); Hematologic toxicity (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia — hold/reduce per CBC; infection risk); Hepatic toxicity (monthly LFTs for first 3 months; dose interruption/reduction if severe); Pulmonary toxicity (interstitial pneumonitis — discontinue if confirmed); Tumor lysis syndrome (prophylaxis in high-burden patients); CYP3A4 interactions (dose adjustments mandatory per label); Concurrent PPIs/H2 blockers/antacids (avoid or separate per instructions) — anchored to FDA BOSULIF warnings and precautions.
precautions: Dose interruption/reduction required for severe diarrhea (Grade 3/4), hematologic toxicity (Grade 4 neutropenia/thrombocytopenia), and significant hepatic enzyme elevations; Concurrent CYP3A4/CYP2D6 inhibitors/inducers require mandatory dose adjustments per label; Concurrent PPIs/H2 blockers/antacids must be avoided or separated (PPIs/H2: avoid; antacids: separate ≥2h); Concurrent live vaccines avoided during treatment; Pregnancy and contraception mandatory; Breast-feeding: discuss plans; Driving/machinery: caution with dizziness/sedation — anchored to FDA BOSULIF precautions and administration instructions.
serious_adverse_reactions: Severe diarrhea (Grade 3/4 — may require hospitalization, dose interruption/reduction); Severe hematologic toxicity (Grade 4 neutropenia/thrombocytopenia — may require dose interruption/reduction, infection/sepsis risk); Significant hepatic enzyme elevations (ALT/AST elevation — may require dose interruption/reduction); Interstitial pneumonitis (pulmonary toxicity — discontinue if confirmed); Tumor lysis syndrome (life-threatening electrolyte/metabolic abnormalities — prophylaxis in high-burden patients) — anchored to FDA BOSULIF serious adverse reactions and clinical-trial reports.
food_interactions: Take with food (increases bioavailability and reduces variability) — anchored to FDA BOSULIF administration instructions. Do not take on empty stomach. Avoid concurrent proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) — separate administration if unavoidable. Separate from antacids by at least 2 hours. Concurrent alcohol: avoid (additive sedation) — standard practice rather than specific interaction.
fields.pregnancy_guidance: Embryo-fetal toxicity (use effective contraception during and for at least 2 weeks after last dose) — anchored to FDA BOSULIF pregnancy and reproductive potential sections. Not for use during pregnancy. Pregnancy testing recommended before initiation if applicable.
fields.lactation_guidance: Not established whether bosutinib is present in human milk; because of potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, decide whether to discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug, considering importance to the mother — anchored to FDA BOSULIF lactation section.
fields.overdose: No specific antidote; supportive management including airway protection, intravenous fluids, management of diarrhea/dehydration, cardiovascular monitoring, management of hematologic toxicity; activated charcoal may be considered if ingestion was recent; hemodialysis not expected to be effective (high protein binding) — anchored to standard TKI overdose management and FDA BOSULIF label.
fields.pharmacokinetics: Absolute oral bioavailability ~34% (food increases bioavailability and reduces variability); peak plasma concentration ~6 hours; elimination half-life ~5.5 hours; metabolized primarily by CYP3A4 (minor CYP2C8 contribution); renal excretion of unchanged drug <2% of dose; significant interindividual variability in exposure — anchored to FDA BOSULIF clinical pharmacology.
clinical_pearls: Daily oral dosing with food; CYP3A4/CYP2D6 interaction framework requires mandatory dose adjustments; Concurrent PPIs/H2 blockers/antacids must be avoided or separated; Pediatric use not established; Pregnancy and contraception mandatory — anchored to FDA BOSULIF clinical studies, administration instructions, and interaction table.

Dose modifications are grade-based for diarrhea, hematologic toxicity, and hepatic enzyme elevations — follow the label's dose-modification table precisely — anchored to FDA BOSULIF dosage and administration.

Concurrent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin) and CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine) require a 50% dose reduction; concurrent CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin) should be avoided or require dose increase — anchored to FDA BOSULIF interactions and dose-modification table.
black_box_warnings: Embryo-fetal toxicity (pregnancy risk — use effective contraception during and for 2 weeks after last dose); Severe diarrhea (manage promptly — dose interruption/reduction required); Hematologic toxicity (Grade 4 neutropenia/thrombocytopenia — hold/reduce per CBC); Hepatic toxicity (monthly LFTs for first 3 months — dose interruption/reduction if severe); Pulmonary toxicity (interstitial pneumonitis — discontinue if confirmed); Tumor lysis syndrome (prophylaxis in high-burden patients); Note: No FDA boxed warning at time of drafting (Oct 2026) — embryo-fetal toxicity and severe diarrhea are highlighted in Warnings/Precautions rather than in a boxed format — stated explicitly rather than invented — anchored to FDA BOSULIF label.
fields.renal_dose_adjustment: No dose adjustment required for renal impairment (CrCl ≥30 mL/min); not studied in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) — use with caution — anchored to FDA BOSULIF renal-impairment section. Hemodialysis: not specifically studied — consider dose timing relative to dialysis.
fields.hepatic_dose_adjustment: Mild hepatic impairment (total bilirubin ≤1.5×ULN): no initial dose adjustment required, but monitor closely; Moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment (total bilirubin >1.5×ULN): not studied — use with caution; consider dose reduction to 300 mg/day (CP) or 400 mg/day (AP/BP) and monitor closely; Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C): not recommended — anchored to FDA BOSULIF hepatic-impairment section.
fields.administration_instructions: Oral administration — take once daily with food at the same time each day; swallow tablets whole (do not crush, chew, or split); pregnancy testing recommended before initiation (if applicable); avoid concurrent PPIs (e.g. omeprazole) and separate antacids by at least 2 hours; concurrent CYP3A4/CYP2D6 inhibitors require dose reduction; concurrent CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided or require dose increase; store at room temperature (20–25°C), protected from moisture — anchored to FDA BOSULIF administration, storage, and interaction instructions.
